query_snapshot: Which categories of material-compatibility considerations does NASA SP-8119 say should be evaluated when selecting metal alloys for contact with a system fluid?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NASA SP-8119 states that metal alloys selected for contact with the system fluid shall be compatible with the system fluid and resistant to all anticipated forms of corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists chemical reaction (including reaction on impact that can cause ignition) between materials and the system fluid as a material-compatibility consideration. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists propellant decomposition (materials or contacts that cause propellant decomposition) as a material-compatibility consideration. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists corrosion modes—atmospheric, galvanic, and stress corrosion—as material-compatibility considerations. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 directs designers to consult the electrochemical series for dissimilar-metal selection and to consider platings and finishes when selecting materials for contact with system fluids. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 54-55, chunk 54bfea7d]
- NASA SP-8119 recommends preparing a list of suitable materials on the basis of the above compatibility, reaction, decomposition, and corrosion considerations (i.e., basing material selection on those evaluated factors). [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 warns against using materials that can cause ignition or propellant decomposition in liquid-oxygen or similar environments (the guidance specifically references avoiding certain materials/contacts in those contexts). [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
